newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says most wanted drug baron caught in Quito.
newsitem.headline: Peru says most wanted drug baron caught in Quito.

text.p: Peruvian authorities said on Monday police had caught the country's most wanted drug trafficker in neighbouring Ecuador.

In a joint sting by Peru's intelligence service and Ecuadoran police, Willer Alvarado Linares was arrested in Quito during the early hours of Sunday morning after he had been tracked from the Colombian capital Bogota.

President Alberto Fujimori described him as the most powerful Peruvian drug lord at large, controlling the traffic of coca leaf, the raw product for cocaine, in the Amazonian regions around the Colombian border.

Justice Minister Carlos Hermoza Moya said Alvarado would be transported to Lima as soon as possible for trial, possibly by a military court for collaboration with guerrillas who operate in Peru's drug-growing regions.

Alvarado's detention was the third major arrest in recent years following the capture in Colombia of fellow Peruvian drug lords Demetrio Chavez Penaherrera, alias "El Vaticano," and Abelardo Cachique Rivera.
Peru, whose economy receives at least $600 million each year from the illegal drugs trade, is the world's largest grower of coca leaf, accounting for fifty percent of total production.
